A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original neural-network training experiments, test accuracies and numerical gradient-alignment calculations.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain original experiments and add ReLU network-width results in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The training algorithms, initialization families, gradient-alignment definition and proposed network components remain unchanged. The added ReLU experiment evaluates an activation already covered by the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate full parity, degree-3 and degree-5 sparse parities, and the polynomial target used for the loss comparison. Online and offline scenarios remain. The added activation/width experiment stays within existing full-parity coverage.

E2.justification: The initialization comparators and L1/L2 loss comparison are retained. In particular, Figure 2 still contains the perturbed-Rademacher curves despite their omission from v2's accompanying description. The new ReLU panel tests model configurations.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a ReLU condition with dimensions 20–60 and widths d^2, d^2.5 and d^3 to the output-layer SGD study. Section 6 also changes Figure 2's stated maximum dimension from 40 to 30, although the plot remains unchanged; this establishes a reporting revision, not a rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a ReLU width-sensitivity analysis examining whether the theoretical sufficient-width bound is tight. The earlier clipped-ReLU analysis, previously Figure 5, remains as its left panel. Other robustness and supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seven random seeds and 95% confidence intervals in Section 6. The added panel follows the existing uncertainty-display practice; no change in run counts or statistical estimation is reported.

E6.justification: The new Figure 9 right panel reports ReLU results: quadratic widths remain below perfect accuracy, while cubic widths reach accuracy 1 over the tested dimensions. All 17 existing plot panels are retained, including the clipped-ReLU results, so this is additional evidence rather than a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Informal Theorem 1 extends its small-perturbation wording to both correlation and hinge losses, whereas v1 explicitly restricted that extension to hinge loss. Informal Theorem 3 narrows to Gaussian initialization and polynomial regimes. The detailed theorems and appendix proofs remain materially unchanged, including the output-layer bound in Lemma 10 and Appendix D.5.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its advertised positive and small-perturbation guarantees from almost-full to full parity. Section 3 presents large-perturbation hardness as an expected extension, unlike v1's established-result summary. However, Theorem 8 and Appendix D still retain that result, making the revised claim presentation inconsistent.

C2.justification: The added ReLU study motivates the conjecture that the d^4 sufficient-width bound could improve to d^3 or d^3.5. The conclusion adds possible applications of gradient alignment to other symmetry and reasoning tasks. The Figure 2 discussion drops the earlier qualification that smaller perturbations were inconclusive.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 removes the explicit perturbed-weight specification for Figure 2's numerical calculation, although those curves remain. Appendix E.2 documents the added ReLU condition. Hardware, framework, general training settings and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds AKM+21, DTA+24 and TDD+24, expands the motivation for parity benchmarks, and includes approximate-message-passing complexity in the related-work discussion. These are limited extensions of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds an introductory motivation paragraph, revises contribution summaries, expands the conclusion and rearranges several Appendix E paragraphs. The overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure 9 with an added ReLU panel. V1 Figures 8 and 9 become v2 Figures 5 and 8. Figures are relocated and the appendix layout becomes more compact, while existing plot content is preserved.

improvement.justification: The added ReLU width study and broader context are useful, but v2 introduces inconsistencies around central guarantees. Section 3 says the output-layer bound is omitted although Lemma 10 and Appendix D.5 retain it, and Figure 2's revised description no longer matches its retained curves and dimension range. These reporting problems outweigh the limited additional empirical support; the underlying proofs and existing results remain largely intact.
